svg.title: Switch vs router: two different forwarding decisions
svg.desc: A switch moves frames inside one network by MAC; a router moves packets between networks by IP prefix
svg.text: Switch vs router: two different forwarding decisions
A switch moves frames inside one network by MAC; a router moves packets between networks by IP prefix
MAC address table (built by watching source MACs)
Dest known → send out one port. Dest unknown / broadcast → flood all ports except ingress.
ROUTER · Layer 3 · routes by IP prefix
ONE PACKET, TWO HOPS · WHAT CHANGES AND WHAT STAYS
Orange = rewritten every hop · Green = end-to-end, never changes · Red = −1 per router
Orange = rewritten every hop · Green = end-to-end, never changes · Red = −1 per router
Switch: same network, MAC table, floods unknowns. Router: different networks, routing table, drops broadcasts.
L3 addresses are end-to-end; L2 addresses are only valid for the current hop.
